framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Ethics > Accountability and responsibility (Practical recommendations and Liability)
requirement_paraphrase: Use assurance techniques to evaluate performance; establish a human-in-the-loop process to oversee and validate outputs in high-impact or high-risk situations; reconsider use if risk is too high; nominate a senior responsible owner.
what_is_tested: Performance assurance; human validation of outputs
who_tests: Not specified; senior responsible owner and human reviewers are named

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Data protection and privacy > Lawfulness and purpose limitation
requirement_paraphrase: The playbook says that before implementing AI solutions a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) is needed; it cites UK GDPR Art. 35(3)(a) as requiring one where AI involves systematic automated evaluation with significant effects, large-scale special category processing or large-scale public monitoring, notes the ICO also requires one for innovative technology processing personal data, says the DPIA should cover each life-cycle stage including training and testing, and that the ICO must be consulted if high risk cannot be mitigated.
what_is_tested: Data protection risk assessment before deployment
who_tests: Controller (public body) with DPO; ICO guidance

framework: UK DSIT Introduction to AI assurance (published 2024-02-12)
clause_or_page: s.4.2 AI assurance mechanisms
requirement_paraphrase: Lists a spectrum of assurance mechanisms - risk assessment, impact assessment, bias audit, compliance audit, conformity assessment (often including performance testing), formal verification - to be used in combination across the AI lifecycle, proportionate to risk.
what_is_tested: Menu of assurance techniques
who_tests: Internal teams or third-party assurance providers

framework: UK Frontier AI Safety Commitments (AI Seoul Summit 2024)
clause_or_page: Commitments II-IV
requirement_paraphrase: Set thresholds at which severe risks are intolerable, assess whether thresholds have been breached, articulate mitigations, and follow explicit processes if thresholds are met, in the extreme not developing or deploying a model if mitigations cannot keep risk below thresholds.
what_is_tested: Severe-risk threshold breach assessment
who_tests: Signatory developers

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Ethics > Fairness, bias and discrimination > Practical recommendations
requirement_paraphrase: Apply bias mitigation and fairness evaluation across the entire AI project life cycle; comply with human rights law, the Equality Act 2010, the Public Sector Equality Duty and EHRC guidance; review outputs and decisions for bias by measuring results for different groups, including intersectional groups; set up feedback routes for unfair decisions or harmful outputs; evaluate continuously as fairness expectations change.
what_is_tested: Bias and fairness of outputs across groups, incl. intersectional
who_tests: Delivery team

who_tests: Developers / security reviewers

framework: US OMB Memorandum M-26-04 (11 December 2025) - Increasing Public Trust in AI Through Unbiased AI Principles
clause_or_page: Agency Actions (a)-(c), p.3; Appendix A s.1 and s.1(A) Minimum Threshold for LLM Transparency, Appendix pp.1-2 of 4
requirement_paraphrase: When procuring an LLM, agencies must obtain enough vendor information to judge compliance with the Unbiased AI Principles; solicitations must at minimum request the acceptable use policy, model/system/data cards (which often include identified risks, mitigations and benchmark evaluation scores), end-user resources and a feedback mechanism. New LLM solicitations must carry contractual compliance requirements, and agency procurement policies had to be updated by 11 March 2026.
what_is_tested: Vendor documentation of LLM risks, mitigations and evaluation results before procurement
who_tests: Procuring agency reviews vendor-supplied documentation; vendor/developer supplies evaluation results

framework: US OMB Memorandum M-26-04 (11 December 2025) - Increasing Public Trust in AI Through Unbiased AI Principles

who_tests: LLM vendor/developer conducts evaluations; agency reviews disclosed results
